trusted_seed.role: trusted C11 artifact used to start the Kofun-written compiler

stage1.role: Kofun-written compiler for the documented nested-block and looping Int/Bool/Text Core subset

selfhost_profile.role: hash-pinned inventory of every language and host feature used by the first canonical compiler S

stage2_frontend_checkpoint.role: Kofun lexer, structural parser, textual IR, and deterministic source projection; not an executable self-recompile

native_checkpoint.role: Kofun-authored ELF64 x86-64 and AArch64 gates; a separate strengthening track from the first C11 fixed point

stage2.implementation: generated compiler produces and reproduces equivalent later generations
stage2.role: three-generation semantic self-hosting fixed point; the first compiler-produced compiler is active separately

fixed_point_closure.criterion: byte equality from generation 2 on - C2 == C3 and A2 == A3 (#271); C1/A1 are hash-pinned runnable provenance

closure_measurement.note: C digests above are deterministic and machine-independent; the executable digests below are the closure measurement on the declared host toolchain, re-proven live by the gate rather than compared against this record

truthful_status: The repository contains a Python-free Kofun-written compiler seed, a frozen first self-host profile, and a compiler-produced compiler that reproduces itself: three generations reach the #271 fixed-point criterion (C2 == C3, A2 == A3) under the selfhost-fixed-point gate. Diverse double compilation (B7, #1136) is closed by the selfhost-diverse-double-compilation gate: two unrelated host C compilers build Kofun compilers that emit byte-identical C and agree on every driver corpus case, so a payload in one host toolchain cannot survive unnoticed. Independent reproduction (B6, #274) remains open, and B7 does not narrow it: both chains run on one machine, one libc, and one kernel, from one checkout, so a payload below the C compiler is shared by both chains and is invisible to this gate.
